Definition: from G1909 and G3727; on oath, i.e. (falsely) a forswearer:--perjured person.
BiblicalUsage: Epiorkos is a perjured person, one who swears falsely — listed by Paul among those for whom the law is made: lawless, disobedient, ungodly, murderers, whoremongers, menstealers, liars, and perjured persons.
TheologicalSignificance: The law names the perjurer because a false oath breaks trust at its root, and trust is what a people runs on.
